solutions.latex:
Let $x$ be the number of blue lollies in the bag

Told that $P(GG)=\dfrac{3}{8}$ and that there are originally 10 Green lollies.

To get $P(GG)$, we start with $\dfrac{10}{x+10}$ for the first selection.

The second selection will be $\dfrac{9}{x+9}$

$$\begin{aligned}\dfrac{10}{x+10}\times\dfrac{9}{x+9}&=\dfrac{3}{8}\\\dfrac{90}{(x+10)(x+9)}&=\dfrac{3}{8}\\720&=3(x+10)(x+9)\\(x+10)(x+9)&=240\\x^2+19x+90&=240\\x^2+19x-150&=0\\(x+25)(x-6)&=0\\\therefore\ x&=6\quad(x>0)\end{aligned}$$

$\therefore$ there are 6 blue lollies in the bag.
solutions.marks_breakdown: 3: Provides correct solution; 2: Forms a quadratic equation or makes significant progress or equivalent merit; 1: Finds an equation for P(GG) using blue and green lollies

solutions.latex:
$$\begin{aligned}y'&=3x^2-6x\\y''&=6x-6\end{aligned}$$

For stationary points, $y'=0$.

$$\begin{aligned}3x^2-6x&=0\\3x(x-2)&=0\\x&=0\ \text{and}\ x=2\end{aligned}$$

For the nature of the stationary points, consider the sign of $y''$.

When $x=0$, $y''=-6$ and $y=0$

$\Rightarrow$ Maximum turning point at $(0,0)$

When $x=2$, $y''=6$ and $y=-4$

$\Rightarrow$ Minimum turning point at $(2,-4)$

solutions.latex:
Points of inflection occur when $y''=0$ AND concavity changes.

$$\begin{aligned}y''&=0\\6x-6&=0\\6x&=6\\x&=1\end{aligned}$$

There is a possible point of inflection where $x=1$

Test concavity:

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|}\hline x&0.5&1&1.5\\\hline y''&-3&0&3\\\hline\end{array}$$

Since concavity changes either side of $x=1$, there is a point of inflection here.

y-coordinate of point of inflection:

$$\begin{aligned}y(1)&=1^3-3(1)^2\\y(1)&=-2\end{aligned}$$

$\therefore$ Point of inflection at $(1,-2)$

solutions.latex:
Volume

$$\begin{aligned}\dfrac{1}{2}\times\dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^3+\pi r^2h&=0.66\pi\\\dfrac{2}{3}r^3+r^2h&=0.66\\2r^3+3r^2h&=\dfrac{99}{50}\\3r^2h&=\dfrac{99}{50}-2r^3\\h&=\dfrac{33}{50r^2}-\dfrac{2r}{3}\end{aligned}$$

Area

$$\begin{aligned}A&=\dfrac{1}{2}\times4\pi r^2+\pi r^2+2\pi rh\\&=2\pi r^2+\pi r^2+2\pi rh\\&=3\pi r^2+2\pi r\left(\dfrac{33}{50r^2}-\dfrac{2r}{3}\right)\\&=3\pi r^2+\dfrac{33\pi}{25r}-\dfrac{4\pi r^2}{3}\\&=\dfrac{33\pi}{25r}+\dfrac{5\pi r^2}{3}\ \text{as required}\end{aligned}$$
solutions.marks_breakdown: 3: Provides correct solution; 2: Finds an equation for the surface area in terms of r (eliminating h); 1: Writes equation for volume incorporating the given volume.

solutions.latex:
$$\begin{aligned}A&=\dfrac{33\pi}{25r}+\dfrac{5\pi r^2}{3}\\&=\dfrac{33\pi}{25}r^{-1}+\dfrac{5\pi}{3}r^2\\A'&=-\dfrac{33\pi}{25}r^{-2}+\dfrac{10\pi}{3}r\\A''&=\dfrac{66\pi}{25}r^{-3}+\dfrac{10\pi}{3}\end{aligned}$$

Min/Max when $A'=0$

$$\begin{aligned}\dfrac{10\pi r}{3}-\dfrac{33\pi}{25r^2}&=0\\\dfrac{10\pi r^3}{3}-\dfrac{33\pi}{25}&=0\\\dfrac{10\pi r^3}{3}&=\dfrac{33\pi}{25}\\r^3&=\dfrac{99}{250}\\\therefore\ r&=\sqrt[3]{\dfrac{99}{250}}\end{aligned}$$

Test whether this will give a minimum or maximum value:

$$\begin{aligned}A''&=\dfrac{66\pi}{25}\left(\sqrt[3]{\dfrac{99}{250}}\right)^{-3}+\dfrac{10\pi}{3}\\&=10\pi\end{aligned}$$

Since $A''>0\Rightarrow$ Min at $r=\sqrt[3]{\dfrac{99}{250}}$

$$\begin{aligned}h&=\dfrac{33}{50r^2}-\dfrac{2r}{3}\\h&=\dfrac{99-100r^3}{150r^2}\\h&=\dfrac{99-100\left(\sqrt[3]{\frac{99}{250}}\right)^3}{150\left(\sqrt[3]{\frac{99}{250}}\right)^2}\\h&=\dfrac{99-100\left(\frac{99}{250}\right)}{150\left(\frac{99}{250}\right)^{\frac{2}{3}}}\\h&=\dfrac{99-\frac{990}{25}}{150}\times\left(\dfrac{99}{250}\right)^{-\frac{2}{3}}\\h&=\dfrac{297}{750}\times\left(\dfrac{99}{250}\right)^{-\frac{2}{3}}\\h&=\left(\dfrac{99}{250}\right)^1\times\left(\dfrac{99}{250}\right)^{-\frac{2}{3}}\\h&=\left(\dfrac{99}{250}\right)^{\frac{1}{3}}\\\therefore\ h&=\sqrt[3]{\dfrac{99}{250}}\end{aligned}$$

$\therefore$ Dimensions are $r=h=\sqrt[3]{\dfrac{99}{250}}$ m

\begin{framed}
Alternate end of solution:

$$\begin{aligned}2r^3+3r^2h&=0.66\\h&=\dfrac{1.98-2r^3}{3r^2}\\h&=\dfrac{1.98-2\left(\sqrt[3]{\frac{99}{250}}\right)^3}{3\left(\sqrt[3]{\frac{99}{250}}\right)^2}\\h&=\dfrac{1.98-\frac{99}{125}}{3}\times\left(\dfrac{99}{250}\right)^{-\frac{2}{3}}\\h&=\dfrac{99}{250}\times\left(\dfrac{99}{250}\right)^{-\frac{2}{3}}\\h&=\left(\dfrac{99}{250}\right)^{\frac{1}{3}}\\\therefore\ h&=\sqrt[3]{\dfrac{99}{250}}\end{aligned}$$
\end{framed}
